fields.h1: Build a Podcast Listener Survey Your Show Can Act On
fields.hero_description: Build a podcast listener survey that listeners open from your show notes, with every answer saved in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: Inside a Listener Survey Built by Emergent
fields.features_subheading: Tell Emergent about your show and what you want to learn. It builds the podcast listener survey, and you change it by prompting.
fields.feature_1:
Questions written around your segments

Name your show, its recurring segments, and the decision you are weighing. Emergent writes the questions to match, and a follow-up prompt rewords, cuts, or adds any of them.
fields.feature_2:
Every answer tied to an episode

Each answer is saved as a row in a database you own, with the episode number you ask it to record. Sort by episode to see which ones listeners rated highest and lowest.
fields.feature_3:
One question per screen on a phone

Listeners who tap the link inside a podcast app land on a phone screen that shows one question at a time, with large answer buttons. Nobody has to zoom through a long form.
fields.feature_4:
A results view for each segment and vote

Emergent builds a results view with the survey: the average for each segment, the count for each choice, and the open comments underneath. Add a chart with another prompt.
fields.feature_5:
Opted-in listeners added to your email list

Send listeners who opt in to your email list or CRM through its API, with their answers attached. The next newsletter can then go only to people who asked for more on a topic.
fields.feature_6:
Your own short link, and code you keep

Custom domains are included in Emergent and use credits, so the survey link read out on air can be short and yours. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository.

fields.tab_content_1:
The sponsor sheet leads with 486 pottery sellers

Every spring, Wet Clay asks the listeners of its pottery podcast who they are and whether they sell their work. Of 1,240 answers, 486 sell at markets or online, 611 make pots as a hobby, and 143 teach classes. The 486 goes on page 1 of the show's sponsor sheet, where clay and glaze suppliers read it first.
fields.tab_content_2:
The news roundup averages 2.9 and leaves the show

Old Roads, a history podcast, puts a rating link in each episode's show notes and asks listeners to score its 4 segments out of 5. Over 6 episodes, the main story averages 4.6 and the listener mailbag 4.4, while the news roundup sits at 2.9. The roundup is dropped, and the mailbag gets its minutes.
fields.tab_content_3:
Listeners vote hiring in as the season 5 theme

Garage Floor, a podcast for small business founders, closes its season with a vote shown one question per screen: which theme should season 5 cover? Of 905 votes, 312 go to hiring a first employee, ahead of pricing at 241. The hosts plan season 5 around hiring and keep pricing for a later season.
fields.tab_content_4:
Small Hours splits its interviews after 402 of 690 answers

Small Hours, a parenting podcast, asks listeners how long an episode should be. Of 690 answers, 402 pick under 30 minutes, and only 87 want more than 45. The show now cuts each 55-minute guest interview into two parts.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Podcast Listener Survey
fields.howto_description: Follow these seven steps to build a podcast listener survey, share it on air, and turn the answers into a change to your show.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Use the names from the show
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Use one scale for every segment
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Pick a link you can say out loud
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down the one choice the survey should settle, such as which segment to drop or what next season covers. Put it at the top of your prompt, and cut any question whose answer cannot change that choice.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Refer to each segment by the name listeners hear on the show, not a working title from your notes. A listener who has never seen your run sheet should know which part of the episode each question means.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Score every segment on the same scale, such as 1 to 5, and keep the wording fixed between rounds. A segment rated out of 5 one month and out of 10 the next cannot be compared. Settle the scale before the first link goes out.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose a short link with no numbers or hyphens. A host can read it on air once and listeners can spell it. Put the same link at the top of the show notes for anyone who would rather tap than type.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Send the survey to 3 listeners who have written in before and ask them to answer on their phones. Note any question they read twice, then fix the wording with a follow-up prompt before launch.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Mention it at the start and the end
fields.howto_step_6_des: Mention the survey near the start of the episode and again at the end, with the link both times. Say how many questions it has before you read the link, and keep that number small enough to say without wincing.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Once the answers are in, say on air what you are changing because of them, such as dropping a segment or picking next season's theme. That is how the people who answered learn their time counted, and it sets up the next survey.

faq_plan.q: What is a podcast listener survey?
faq_plan.a: A podcast listener survey is a short set of questions a show sends its own audience about the show: which episodes and segments land, what to cover next, and who is listening. Hosts link it from the show notes or read the link on air, then use the answers to plan episodes and pitch sponsors.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a podcast listener survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe your show, its segments, and the decision the answers should settle in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder. Emergent builds the survey and the database behind it. Put the link in your show notes, read it out on the next episode, and change any question with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a podcast listener survey ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask about the show first, then about the listener. Which recent episode did you like most? Which segment would you skip? What topic should the show cover next? For a sponsor profile, add what the listener does and what they buy for the hobby the show covers. End with one open question for anything else.

faq_plan.q: How can a podcast listener survey let listeners rank topics for next season?
faq_plan.a: Give listeners 4 to 6 candidate topics and ask them to put the list in order, top choice first. A ranking survey shows which topics come second and third, not only the winner, which helps when a season has room for more than one theme. On a phone, a single pick is quicker to answer than a full ranking.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a podcast listener survey have?
faq_plan.a: About 8 for a yearly survey, and 1 to 3 for a rating linked from one episode's show notes. Tell listeners the count on air, and put any sponsor profile questions last and make them optional. A survey Emergent builds can show one question per screen, which keeps an 8-question survey readable on a phone.

faq_plan.q: Where should I share a podcast listener survey?
faq_plan.a: Share it in the episode itself, in the show notes, and in your newsletter if the show has one. Pin it in any listener community the show runs, and leave it open for 2 to 3 weeks for people who listen late. There are no response caps on a survey Emergent builds, even when an old episode picks up new listeners.

faq_plan.q: Can a podcast listener survey include a few fun questions?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add one or two near the end: a light question, such as which past guest a listener would invite to dinner, suits an easygoing show and gives the host something to read on air. Keep the rated questions plain and save the jokes for last. A list of funny survey questions is a good place to borrow from.

faq_plan.q: How do I use podcast listener survey results in a sponsor pitch?
faq_plan.a: Lead with the one number that matches the sponsor's customer, such as how many listeners sell their own work, and say how many people answered and in which month. Share totals, never individual answers. With Emergent, every answer sits in a database you own, and a new count for a different sponsor takes one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: How often should I run a podcast listener survey?
faq_plan.a: Once a year for the full survey, plus a short rating in the show notes whenever you try a new segment. Run the yearly survey in the same month each time, and keep its questions the same, so this year's numbers line up with last year's. Skip a round if nothing on the show has changed.

faq_plan.q: Should a podcast listener survey use yes or no questions?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for single checks: would you want a bonus episode, should the mailbag stay, did you hear the last 3 episodes? Each is one tap on a phone and easy to count. Use a scale instead when you want to track a score over time. A yes no questions survey works well as a quick check between yearly surveys.

plan.angle: No top 10 in the workbook (Wave 3) and every AlsoAsked candidate drifts to podcast rankings, listener counts and podcast income, so the searcher is a host or producer who wants to ask their own audience something and act on it. Question lists stop at the list. This page shows four podcast listener surveys built from a prompt, each ending in one decision about the show: a pottery podcast putting a listener figure in its sponsor sheet, a history podcast cutting its lowest-rated segment, a founders podcast letting listeners pick next season's theme, and a parenting podcast splitting long interviews after listeners ask for shorter episodes. The FAQ covers questions, ranking topics, length, where to share the link, a light tone, sponsor pitches, how often to ask and yes or no questions, as plain advice with no third-party claims.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Podcast Listener Survey Your Show Can Act On'; hero 'Build a podcast listener survey that listeners open from your show notes, with every answer saved in a database you own.' covers the whole job, no sibling topic.

intent.evidence: No top 10 in the workbook; every AlsoAsked candidate drifts (all x). The page serves a host who wants to ask the audience: four worked surveys (sponsor profile, segment ratings, season vote, episode length), sample questions in FAQ 3 ('Which recent episode did you like most? Which segment would you skip?'), counts, cadence, sharing and a 7-step how-to. Meta promise (sponsors, segments, season theme, episode length) is delivered tab by tab.

specificity.evidence: Podcast vocabulary throughout: 'show notes', 'run sheet', 'read it on air', 'sponsor sheet', 'mailbag'. Step 4 'Choose a short link with no numbers or hyphens. A host can read it on air once and listeners can spell it.'

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'Name your show, its recurring segments...', 'Each answer is saved as a row...', 'Every spring, Wet Clay asks...', 'Old Roads, a history podcast, puts a rating link...'.

craft.evidence: Short declaratives, numbers that add up (486+611+143=1,240; 312+241+208+144=905; 402+201+87=690). Two ', so' endings (feature_6, FAQ 9) logged as a note; under the QC block threshold.

voice.evidence: Reads like an operator: 'keep that number small enough to say without wincing', 'That is how the people who answered learn their time counted'. No hype verbs, no triplet padding.

truth.evidence: Emergent sentences map to claims_used: prompt-build (results view, 'a follow-up prompt rewords, cuts, or adds'), database-owned, conversational ('one question at a time'), api-connect ('to your email list or CRM through its API'), custom-domain ('included in Emergent and use credits'), code-export ('On paid plans'), no-caps. No third-party, legal or statistical fact stated; plan.claims_to_source is empty and nothing needs one. Table is library-generated (QC V2/V3 pass).

distinct.evidence: Own stories (Wet Clay, Old Roads, Garage Floor, Small Hours) and podcast-only how-to (read the link on air, mention it at the start and end); not a sibling with nouns swapped. Sibling primaries appear only as FAQ links (ranking survey, funny survey questions, yes no questions survey).

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic written questions, each answered in its first sentence ('About 8 for a yearly survey...', 'Once a year for the full survey...'); hub link in item 2; 3 sibling links; moat lines in items 5, 6 and 8 use approved claims only; no brand or file-format asks; paa gate 10 pass, 0 reject, 0 flag.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches copy: Wet Clay 486/611/143 of 1,240 and 'Sponsor sheet, page 1'; Old Roads 4.6/4.4/2.9 'Last 6 episodes'; Garage Floor 'Hiring: 312 of 905', 'Pricing: 241'; Small Hours 402/201/87 of 690, cover 58% (402/690). One hero per tab, cursor on the button.
